> The Tropical Fruit Bowl, designed to be packed with sensors so that I have a board with interesting readings. The board will be able to detect humidity, temperature, pressure, movement, and air quality in ppm. I will include a rotary encoder, slider and two buttons to navigate the firmware that I will build to show these cool sensors as graphs.

## Design

### 2026-10-29: Ok so, this is the Tropical Fruit Bowl PCB I'm building. I am going to challenge myself this week, in which I combine elements from Starbie and the MIDI Keyboard along with a new sensor component to c

**5h**

Ok so, this is the Tropical Fruit Bowl PCB I'm building. I am going to challenge myself this week, in which I combine elements from Starbie and the MIDI Keyboard along with a new sensor component to create something not foun d in any guides from Hack Club. The main feature is the new ENS160+AHT21 module that detects air quality in ppm and I decided to add a rotary encoder, a slider, and two buttons so that I can navigate and play with the UI I will build later. I'm planning to spend the most time designing the firmware, because the hardware part is pretty easy. I'd have to master C++ or circuit python for this one.

### 2026-10-30: This part went by pretty fast, because I became fluent with PCB component layouts and wiring. It's actually pretty easy to do once you figure out the schematic part, just draw and plug in the wires. I

**3h**

This part went by pretty fast, because I became fluent with PCB component layouts and wiring. It's actually pretty easy to do once you figure out the schematic part, just draw and plug in the wires. I then had to go find a custom 3D model for my new ppm air sensor but that was also pretty easy. I cycled through many draft designs before settling on this design. I also added some decorations which turned out to be pretty easy to add once I understood everything for the image converter.
